data.body:
Remediation epic progress: 3/14 closed (F1, F13, F12 — all merged), 2 pushed and awaiting review (F3 = change 2530, F5 = change 2531), 9 open.

F3 (contiguous-industrial-dugong): the plan-review type exemption had SIX masters and nothing asserted they partition TicketType, so an eighth type would be neither gated nor exempted — silently deciding whether the claim gate runs. Declared once in rebar.types beside TicketType (a true leaf, only `typing` imported, so every consumer reaches it without a cycle) and DERIVED the complement. Corrected three comments, one of which had drifted materially: composer cited orchestrator:560 as a "bug/session_log short-circuit before P9", but that literal sits in the attestation DRIFT-REFRESH path.

Scope discipline worth recording: my no-relist test initially flagged composer's `_TYPES` — the full member list. That IS a mirror, but a different one, with its own ticket in this epic (F7, boiling-gold-pterosaurs), and it is a distinct concept (every valid type to CREATE, not the gate's exemption). Narrowed the assertion to PROPER subsets rather than fixing it here, which would have put the change beyond its plan. Both mutants killed.

F5 (feedable-clannish-mite): the MCP model/schema drift gate was a property-NAME set difference that never read `enum`, over a hand-listed registry covering 11 of 32 public *Out models. Derived the registry (a model is covered when its snake_case schema file exists) and added enum-VALUE comparison. No enum mismatch exists today, so that half is preventive; the tests seed divergence in both directions rather than asserting an empty result.

Deriving the registry surfaced REAL drift: 4 models, 41 undeclared canonical properties (TicketStateOut 23, NextBatchOut 12, GateResultOut 5, CreateResultOut 1). Declaring those fields changes the MCP tools' published outputSchema — the wire contract clients read — so bundling them into a gate refactor would be both large and risky. Baselined against a new ticket, lowly-lawrencium-ovenbird (3a02-66ea-9229-470c), linked discovered_from F5, with the ratchet shape the complexity and mechanism gates already use: green at rest, any NEW omission fails, entries drain as that ticket lands.

PROCESS LESSON, cost three re-reviews: set file_impact BEFORE running review-plan. Setting it after invalidates the attestation (`file_impact 0 -> N paths`), and sign-review correctly refuses to re-sign across a changed plan. F3 and F5 had their file_impact recorded up front.

Also of note: closing a BUG ticket requires --class. F12 closed as `preexisting` — the doc drift predates this epic.
